correctness.rationale: Let L_j=(log(j+e))^2 and B_n=product_{j<=n}L_j. Uniform-disk independent coefficients xi_n give a normally convergent entire f=sum xi_n B_n z^n/n!. For fixed compact annulus 0<delta<=|z|<=R, splitting derivative F_n into m<=n and m>n gives |F_n(z)|<=2B_n exp(R L_{2n}) eventually; choosing m=floor(|z|L_n) yields one coefficient size >=B_n exp(|z|L_n-1)/(3 sqrt(|z|L_n)). Conditional planar-disk area anti-concentration implies P{logB_n+|z|L_n-log|F_n(z)| > H_n+s}<=e^(-2s), H_n=3+log(1+R L_n), and E exp(positive deficit)<=2. Jensen on a centered circle gives P{average deficit>=t}<=2e^-t. On a zero-free disk harmonic log|F_n| has mean equal to its central value, forcing average deficit >=gamma(c,r)L_n-|c|(L_{2n}-L_n)-H_n-log2, with gamma(c,r)>0 from strict subharmonicity of |z| off zero. Since L_n~log^2 n and L_{2n}-L_n=O(log n), the zero-free event has probability <=2exp(-c log^2 n), summable. Borel–Cantelli on a countable rational disk base gives every nonempty open U a zero of every sufficiently high derivative. Coefficient order formula and infinitely many |xi_n|>=1/2 give order exactly one, while B_n^(1/n)~(log n)^2 makes type infinite. Conversely finite exponential type bounds b_n=g^(n)(0) by O(sqrt(n)tau^n); for lambda>tau choose r with e^(lambda r)-1<1, and maximizing |b_n|/lambda^n at each large tail implies g^(n) has no zero in fixed B(0,r), contradicting cofinite zero-hitting. The all-order probability and maximal-coefficient proof is mathematical, not finite sampling. No deterministic realization or effective N(U) follows.
